newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans set 8-1/2-year high, end limit up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans set 8-1/2-year high, end limit up.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures set 8-1/2-year highs and nearby months ended limit up on ideas USDA will cut its 1996-97 ending stocks estimate, raising concerns supplies will not last through the summer.
Floor sources said buying pools in the May contract totaled four million bushels and in the July, three million.
Analysts predicted USDA would trim its ending stocks estimate by 10 million to 15 million bushels in Tuesday's report. USDA in February put stocks at 140 million bushels.
"A lot of people are looking for a cut in ending stocks and they better get it at these prices," a trader said.
The March contract set an 8-1/2 year high for a nearby contract at $8.62 a bushel, topping the $8.44 mark set in the week of September 23, 1988.
Traders said volume on the day was not as heavy as it was last week but few sellers could be found. The largest play on the day was in soybean options, they said.
Smith Barney reportedly bought 3,000 May $9.25 calls and 4,000 July $10.00 calls early in the rally which prompted increased buying interest in the futures.
Soybeans ended 30-1/4 to five cents per bushel higher with limitless March up 30-1/4 at $8.57-3/4 a bushel.
